THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.6162/2009, dated 25.09.2012 on the file of the VII Additional Judge, Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes,
Bangalore.

entities.text:
VII Additional Judge, Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes,
Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.8,00,000/- an account of the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the case of the claimant is that, on 21.11.2008 he was walking on the left side of the road to go to his office and at that time a Maruti Omni dashed against the claimant, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver and he sustained injuries and spent an amount of Rs.75,000/-
towards medical expenses.
Due to the said injuries he could not work as earlier.

It is the case NC:
2023:KHC:33145 of the claimant that, the driver of the offending vehicle was having valid driving license.
3. It is the case of the Insurance Company that, the driver of the offending vehicle was authorised to live the LMV non transport vehicle.
He was not holding license to drive LMV transport vehicle and as the vehicle is a LMV transport vehicle, the Court below held that, there was violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Considering the injuries sustained by the claimant granted an amount of Rs.2,75,845/- as compensation payable by the owner of the vehicle.
4. There is no representation on behalf of the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that, the judgment in the case of Mukund Devagan V/s Oriental Insurance Company1 is referred to the larger Bench and it is coming up for AIR 2017 SC 3668 NC: 2023:KHC:33145 hearing before the Hon'ble Apex Court and as such the matter may be adjourned.

entities.text: Mukund Devagan V/s Oriental Insurance Company1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Several matters have been adjourned nearly for a month.

It is submitted that, para No.59 of the said judgment reads as follows:-
59.
Section 10 of the Act requires a driver to hold a licence with respect to the class of vehicles and not with respect to the type of vehicles.

In one class of vehicles, there Smt Subba Lakshmi Sanathkumar vs S T Gangadaraiah on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143220800/
2 may be different kinds of vehicles.

entities.text: Smt Subba Lakshmi Sanathkumar vs S T Gangadaraiah
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.
As light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle also, a holder of light motor vehicle licence can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
It was pre- amended position as well the post-amended position of Form 4 as amended on 28.3.2001.

Any other interpretation would be repugnant to the definition of "light motor vehicle" in section 2(21) and the provisions of section 10(2)(d), Rule 8 of the Rules of 1989, other provisions and also the forms which are in tune with the provisions.

Even otherwise the forms never intended to exclude transport vehicles from the category of 'light motor vehicles' and for light motor vehicle, the validity NC: 2023:KHC:33145 period of such licence hold good and apply for the transport vehicle of such class also

and the expression in Section 10(2)(e) of the Act 'Transport Vehicle' would include medium goods vehicle, medium passenger motor vehicle, heavy goods vehicle, heavy passenger motor vehicle which earlier found place in section 10(2)(e) to (h) and our conclusion is fortified by the syllabus and rules which we have discussed.
6. In that view of the matter the only issue that falls for consideration before this Court is whether the Court below was right in holding that, though he was having a driving licence to drive the LMV non transport vehicle but he was driving a LMV transport vehicle.
In the light of law laid down in Mukund Devagan case Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
1) The respondent - insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
2) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified NC: 2023:KHC:33145 copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
3) No costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

SD/-
